also: give it a coat of paint

evidence: Cic. Div. 1.23: aspersa temere pigmenta in tabulā (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: coat, spread over: paint (a wall, a door) with a colour
terms.grammar: the thing coated in the accusative, the coating in the ablative (postēs pice); or the coating in the accusative and the thing in the dative (parietī cēram)
evidence: Plaut. Most. 827: sī sunt inductī pice
Plin. NH 33.122: parietī cēram liquefactam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: pingō paints a picture; a wall or a door is coated with a colour, indūcere.

phrases.english: Come on, let’s paint the Easter eggs!

phrases.latin: Quō colōre hoc ōvum pingis? — Rubrō.
phrases.english: What colour are you painting this egg? — Red.

phrases.latin: dīcō esse ex quā tantum tēctōrium vetus dējectum sit et novum inductum. Quodsī tantā pecūniā columnās dealbārī putāssem, certē numquam aedīlitātem petīvissem.
phrases.english: I say there is one from which only the old coating was knocked off and a new one put on. If I had thought it cost so much to whitewash columns, I should never have stood for the aedileship.

phrases.latin: atque etiam nunc satis bonī sunt, sī sunt inductī pice
phrases.english: and they’re good enough even now, if they’re given a coat of pitch

sources: Lewis & Short: pingo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 52, 168.
